children: President Donald Trump has said he's not opposed to Chinese automakers manufacturing ​cars in the U.S. as long as they employ Americans.
"If China wanted to come in and open a plant to build their cars here, I'd be okay with that," Trump said in an interview with
. "Japan does it, but they hire our people. The ​big thing is they hire our people."
"What I don't want is them to build in Mexico and just, you know, build it inexpensively and ship it across the border," he clarified.

With Trump scheduled to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping later this month, Sen. ​Elissa Slotkin (D-MI) said there were "rumors that Trump is planning to allow Chinese cars to be sold in the U.S. as part of a larger deal he's putting together," adding that it "would be a strategic mistake."

"She made it up," Trump said about Slotkin's comments. "It's a total phony rumor. I'm the one that has 150% tariff on any car from China. You know how many Chinese cars we have in the United States? None."
U.S. automakers have called on Congress to pass legislation that would ​permanently ban ⁠Chinese vehicles from the U.S. market.

"Right now, Chinese automakers are dumping subsidized vehicles with connected software and hardware around the world," Alliance for Automotive Innovation CEO John Bozzella wrote to congressional leadership, warning that these vehicles are capable of collecting and transmitting sensitive data to the Chinese Communist Party.
"This hasn't happened inside the U.S. yet, but given the scale and urgency of this threat, we urge you to enact a Chinese vehicle, software and hardware ban before adjourning this year," he added.
